newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish debt made another jump ahead to new highs on Monday, drawing strength from the EU Ecofin's approval of Spain's convergence plan and from expectations for an official rate cut this week, dealers said.
Though scared by the new peaks, traders added that the market did not seem any more cautious this week.
"Everybody would prefer it to stop, but it doesn't," said Jose Ramon Arechederra, dealer at ABN Amro in Madrid. "If you stay out you lose money, so you can't".
The peseta, which was earlier worrying bonos, recovered ground to end around Friday's closing level at 84.57/59.
But others were more careful, saying uncertainty from abroad, such as the French vote or U.S. Federal Reserve policy, were keeping further rallies on hold.
"At the end of May we'll have a more clear outlook and we could take position, and stop doing intra-day trading like we are now," Arechederra added.
The expectations of a tame April CPI figure on Wednesday, with the inflation rate expected to fall to around 1.9 percent year on year, were already priced in, dealers said.
They also said that a possible official rate cut by 25 basis points to 5.25 pct on Friday, was already factored into prices.
